ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Step 7: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "downstream timeout or slow query handling and mitigation"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for handling downstream timeouts or slow queries.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-13-8 (match score 9.1).
  [R-13-8] DNS resolution failures - Related runbooks (match score 9.1): If connections work but replies are slow, use the downstream dependency timeout runbook. If requests are turned away because healthy servers are overloaded, use the traffic spike runbook instead of this one.
  [R-12-8] Database connection leak audit - Related runbooks (match score 7.3): For an acute outage with all connections in use, use the connection pool exhaustion runbook. For one very slow query, use the slow query runbook. This audit is only for slow drift, so do not start it during an incident.
  [R-03-1] Slow query or missing index - Summary (match score 6.4): Requests to the database are slow. A query that used to be fast now takes seconds, usually because an index is missing or is no longer being used, and every request that depends on that query waits for it.

Previous hypotheses:
- downstream_timeout: Requests in notifications are timing out or failing with 500/502 errors when calling /api/v1/pay, with durations reaching tens of seconds. (evidence: M-032, L-0289, L-0304)
- slow_query_missing_index: High request durations and 500 errors occurring on specific endpoints without corresponding errors in the dependency service suggest database queries might be taking too long. (evidence: L-0289, L-0304)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: Long request durations leading to timeouts and 502/500 errors can be caused by database connection pools becoming fully utilized under load. (evidence: L-0289, L-0290)
